resolution: Diagnostic + spec thread on the Studio UV live preview vs Blockbench, driven by the user across many side-by-side frames. Root cause established and grounded in source: our editMesh.ts unwrapMesh() re-derives UVs from the LIVE mesh every render (box-projection by dominant normal, sized to current face dims, shelf-packed), so UVs mutate on every vertex/edge edit and never form a stable atlas — whereas Blockbench stores UVs as per-corner DATA in a fixed square texture space, assigned once and sticky, restructuring only on TOPOLOGY change (a loop cut subdivides within the parent's UV rectangle; shared-edge cut verts create boundary notches on neighbor islands; the UV editor is selection-scoped). The why: the UV atlas IS the paintable texture — paint surface + image-to-image export guide + sampled texture on the mesh — so a live-derived atlas can never be painted/generated against. Locked the corrected model and a four-phase build (5a stored per-corner UVs + selection-scoped panel rewrite; 5b one square atlas + guide export; 5c route the existing painter at the atlas + bake content-addressed via game/textures; 5d image-to-image) into cart/hmsc-int/editors/MESH_EDITOR_PLAYBOOK.md Part 5, per the design gate. No code yet — Phase 5a is the next build, pending the user's green light. Nothing committed.
